newsitem.title: USA: Herman Miller boosts share repurchases.
newsitem.headline: Herman Miller boosts share repurchases.

text.p: Herman Miller Inc said Friday that its board of directors approved the repurchase of an additional two million shares for the company's common stock repurchase program.
The office furniture systems maker said it also has finalized the previously announced disposal of its German manufacturing operations.
During fiscal 1997, Herman Miller said it has purchased, on a split-adjusted basis, 3.95 million shares for a total of $95 million at an average price of $23.94 per share.

The new two-million share authorization, combined with the remaining shares from the July 1996 authorization, will allow the company to continue to return cash to shareholders through stock repurchases and is an indication of optimism, Herman Miller Chief Financial Officer Brian Walker said in a statement.
The company also completed the transfer of 100 percent of the common stock of the company's German subsidiary to Dietrich Muller, a German entrepreneur.
Muller operates two other furniture companies in Germany and has extensive restructuring experience, Herman Miller said.

The transfer to Muller was completed after Herman Miller repaid all of the outstanding bank debt of its German subsidiary and transferred $3 million to the subsidiary as a precondition of the transaction.

"The acquisition by Mr. Muller greatly increases the employees' prospects for continued employment," Walker said. "This transaction will not have a material impact on the fourth quarter results. Provisions taken in the third quarter to write down the net assets of our German manufacturing operations to their net realizable value and other associated costs will be sufficient."

As stated in the earlier announcement, Herman Miller will maintain a small team to continue serving existing multinational clients in Germany, eastern Europe, and the Netherlands, which will focus on the sale of Herman Miller brand products manufactured in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Italy.
